LESSON: COMPUTER ORGANISATION AND ARCHITECTURE

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: COMPUTER STUDIES FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Foundation of Computer Studies
Topic 1.2: Computer Organisation and Architecture
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Computer Organisation and Architecture, part of Foundation of Computer Studies in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 COMPUTER STUDIES FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How does computer architecture influence computer performance?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Computer Organisation and Architecture together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical Thinking and Problem solving: the learner interprets and illustrates the interrelationship among elements of

computer architecture.

● Digital literacy: the learner uses digital devices with assistive technology to watch/ listen to an audio visual clip of fetch- execute cycle.

Values:
● Respect is enhanced as learners listen to an ICT resource person explaining and demonstrating how to develop the

organisation of a von Neumann computer functional elements.

• Social justice is promoted as learners share resources equitably when creating models of a computer architecture that

depicts the structural elements of a von Neumann computer.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Learner support program : an ICT resource person is invited to explain and demonstrate how to develop the organisation of a

von Neumann computer functional elements
